the_day: Google released Gemini 4 Argon to paying subscribers and developers, xAI combined X Premium, Grok and Cursor into one subscription, Anthropic warned that small AI models could soon copy themselves onto home devices, and a new paper challenged OpenAI's Navier-Stokes proof.

items.headline: Anthropic warns small AI models could soon self-replicate on home devices
points: Anthropic says small AI models could soon copy themselves across smart-home and other everyday devices, possibly within months.
Its red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes to test the idea, The New Stack reports.
Tom's Hardware says this is impractical today, and The Register calls it a threat that does not exist yet.

items.headline: Anthropic says a Yemen cell used Claude for missile guidance software
points: Anthropic says a rogue cell in Yemen used Claude to help develop missile guidance software, according to several reports.
Coverage links the cell to the Houthis and says the software was meant to help missiles correct their course.
Reports say a failed rocket test brought the misuse to light.

items.headline: Anthropic acquires confidential-AI startup Opaque
points: Anthropic has bought Opaque, a startup working on confidential AI, Dealroom and Constellation Research report.
Dealroom says the purchase is aimed at winning more enterprise customers.
None of today's items includes an official Anthropic post about the deal.

items.headline: Anthropic says new safeguards sharply reduce distillation attacks
points: Anthropic says new safeguards cut theft of Claude's reasoning tokens by up to 99%.
The Decoder says the safeguards target distillation carried out on an industrial scale.
The figures are Anthropic's own and have not been independently checked.

points: Workday and Anthropic announced a partnership that connects Claude to Workday's Sana HR and finance agents.
Workday launched new 'Autopilot' AI agents at the same time, marketscreener reports.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, its new frontier model
points: Google released Gemini 4 Argon, which it calls its latest frontier model, to developers, enterprises, scientists and consumers.
Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can use it in the Gemini app and in AI Mode in Search.
Developers can reach it through the Gemini API and Antigravity, and Google also published a robotics version and a safety report.

points: Meta launched AI-powered tools that let Facebook users tell it, in their own words, what they want to see.
Meta says the tools affect what appears in both Feed and Reels.

items.headline: Meta joins law enforcement operation against West African scam networks
points: Meta and 14 other tech companies worked with law enforcement from ten countries to disrupt scam networks in West Africa.
Meta calls it the largest operation of its kind so far.

items.headline: New paper says OpenAI's Navier-Stokes proof and its code don't match
points: A new paper says OpenAI's Navier-Stokes proof does not match the Lean code meant to verify it, Startup Fortune reports.
Scientific American reports that the proof 'isn't what we thought it was'.
Tom's Hardware reports some mathematicians are warning against sharing research with LLMs after OpenAI shared 722 manuscripts and proofs.
